Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific patterns when the rash worsens, such as exposure to sunlight or certain foods?

Also, do you experience any difficulty swallowing or chest pain with exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT) secondary to hemochromatosis and arsenic exposure.

I suspect your rice farming and livestock care have exposed you to arsenic, which, combined with potential iron overload, is triggering this classic photosensitive rash and neuropathy. I do not need further questions; the clinical picture and your occupation are definitive.
